b/d

*Following nitcion's opinion - expressed with regard to Putonghua (which I do not share) - [[b|b]]  (and still other consonants),  in Spanish ought to be dropped, since they do not have an equivalent in Lojban: [[b|b]] ist pronounced more like a bilabial [[jbocre: v|v]] rather than a plosive, {d} is not a dental stop, but kind of dental fricative(?) like in English [[jbocre: then|then]]. As nitcion surely knows, this is not totally different from modern Greek dhelta and bheta (using the Sindarin way of literation). Should we also drop [[b|b]] and [[d|d]] then from a Greek pronunciation list (maybe still to come)? ''[[jbocre: pne|pne]]'d say no, because (modern) Greek '''has''' those sounds -- it simply spells them {mp} and {nt}, respectively.'' Yet, accepting this idea, what would be the use of all those lists? There's hardly any foreign (i.e. "non-lojban) language whose phonologic state matches exactly with Lojban.  If not just for the convenience of those native speakers (giving them a faint idea of how Lojban is to be pronounced), wouldn't it be more helpful (from a scientistic aspect) to  only give a list referring to the _exact_ pronunciation, which BTW exists already in the Book. I'm not sure how Spanish [[jbocre: v|v]] (vaca) is pronounced: Is it dento-labial?  ''--.aulun.''
**b and v are normally a bilabial fricative, but sometimes they can be a bilabial plosive. They can also be a labiodental fricative in emphatic speech, or as a (somewhat artificial) way to distinguish v from b. If 'b' is removed from the list then 'd' and 'g' should also be removed, as they are also normally fricative, not plosive. --[[User:xorxes|xorxes]]

***A few months ago, I decided not to put up with my pronouncing everything like a gringo anymore. So I studied the pronunciation of these sounds on Shakira recordings, and my analysis is this: In Colombia, at least v/b is v intervocalically (abeja would thus be Lojban avexa) and b elsewhere (making vaca a Lojban baka). D is dh intervocalically (cadhena), before r (padhre), or word-finally (redh). It is d elsewhere (eg, de). I assume that other dialects have their own patterns. - mi'e. [[jbocre: .kreig.daniyl.|.kreig.daniyl.]]
